Thanks — initial triage from runtime team below. Short summary:
- We see a high-latency tail in short sequences after xz9.v3 was pushed. The kernel profiling indicates a 10–12% increase in mean token overhead for the hotpath kernels in GPUs used in us-west2.
- Error rates are unchanged (good), so this looks like a performance regression, not a correctness bug.
- Preliminary correlation with a compilation pipeline change that adjusted kernel tiling heuristics for sequence length <=64.

Immediate mitigations we can execute within 60–90 minutes with standard runbooks:
1) Canary rollback: route 10% of OptiCore hotpath traffic to xz9.v2 for 30 minutes and monitor p95.
2) Fallback routing: enable model-level fallback so requests that exceed 500ms are re-routed to xz9.v2 automatically (will increase cost).
3) Full rollback: if canary shows improvement, we can roll back all traffic on us-west2 to xz9.v2 — needs ops window and approval.

Risks: KV cache warmup and prefix cache miss storms after rollback can temporarily increase tail latency for the first ~5 minutes. We'll include warming steps in the playbook.

I'll prepare traces and a proposed rollback playbook. Need explicit approval from Michael for a full rollback and authorization to notify the customer about an SLA carveout if we keep xz9.v3 live during investigation.

-Rishi
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
